einzeiler: Ron Howard reflects on his directing career, childhood memories, and classic Hollywood.
kurzfassung: Ben Mankiewicz sits down with director and former child star Ron Howard to discuss his transition behind the camera. Howard shares stories from working with legends like John Wayne, Bette Davis, and Robert De Niro. They also explore his creative process, cinematic influences, and favorite film memories.
stichpunkte: Transitioning from acting on Happy Days and The Andy Griffith Show to a successful directing career
Overcoming early career anxiety by reading Frank Capra's autobiography and adopting a diverse genre approach
Learning the nuances of staging and visual storytelling from cinematographer Don Peterman on Splash
Navigating a tense atmosphere and feuding personalities on the set of The Shootist with John Wayne and Don Siegel
Directing Bette Davis in Skyward and handling her initial skepticism about working with a young novice actor
Observing Robert De Niro's intense physical and behavioral research methods during the production of Backdraft
Recalling early moviegoing experiences with his father Rance Howard, including seeing B-Westerns and classic dramas
Reflecting on underappreciated directorial efforts like The Paper, The Missing, and Eden

clips.hook: Treating a directing career like a television season
clips.text: Deciding to model a long-term filmmaking career after a television schedule helped manage the fear of failure by accepting that not every project will be a massive hit.

clips.hook: Running lines with a reluctant John Wayne
clips.text: Finding a way to build rapport with a major star by simply asking to practice dialogue when no one else dared to approach him.

clips.hook: An unexpected gesture of approval from Bette Davis
clips.text: Earning the respect of a legendary actress after a grueling first day of shooting resulted in a surprising physical sign of validation.

clips.hook: Studying firefighters to build authentic characters
clips.text: Watching Robert De Niro intensely shadow real-life investigators and absorb their mannerisms deeply inspired future character direction.

clips.hook: The ultimate movie prop to steal
clips.text: Choosing a very specific, sentimental musical instrument used by Andy Griffith as the ultimate item to take from a hypothetical prop warehouse.

beschreibung:
Oscar-winning director Ron Howard tells host Ben Mankiewicz that he feared being “branded” a supernatural comedy director following the success of “Splash” and “Cocoon.” After tapping guidance from his “Happy Days” boss, Garry Marshall, and insight from Frank Capra’s biography, Howard set forth to explore the medium of film in all its genres as a director. He tells Ben about being mesmerized by “Bonnie and Clyde” and “The Graduate” and learning how to work with stars when acting in “The Shootist” with John Wayne directed by Don Siegel. Ron Howard’s Super 8 answers run the gamut from nods to “Project Hail Mary.” and “Eastern Promises,” to “One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest,” and “Blazing Saddles.”
